title: Through, Bounce or Block?
source: Science G3 B2 Study sheet pp.7-11; Worksheet Q3-Q7

scenes.t: Why can we see through a window but not through a wall? Materials let different amounts of light pass through them.
Transparent materials let most light pass through. We can see clearly through them, like clear glass, clear water and clear plastic.
Translucent materials let some light pass through. We can see through them, but not clearly, like parchment paper, linen curtains and a frosted bulb.
Opaque materials let no light pass through. We cannot see through them at all, like wood, ceramic and aluminum.
Reflection is when light bounces back from a surface. We see things because light bounces off them and travels into our eyes.
Smooth, shiny surfaces like mirrors, water, metal, foil and jewelry reflect the most light. Light hits a mirror and bounces off at the same angle.
Rubber, matte paint and some fabrics are non-reflective. They do not reflect light well.
Reflective strips on coats help firefighters and builders be seen at night. Solar power stations use mirrors to collect sunlight. But in a totally dark room you cannot see a mirror!

items.a: Lets most light through; we see clearly. Clear glass, water.
Lets some light through; we see unclearly. Parchment paper.
Lets no light through. Wood, ceramic, aluminum.
Light bouncing back from a surface.
Mirror, water, foil, jewelry, some metals.
Helps people be seen at night.
Light bounces off objects into our eyes.

why.r: Smooth and shiny surfaces reflect the most light.
why.n: It does not reflect light well.

activities.title: Torch Detective
activities.goal: Test which materials let light through, and catch a reflection.
activities.safe: Never shine light into anyone's eyes.

predict.q: Which one will let the MOST light through?

steps.t: Make the room dark and shine the torch on a wall.
Hold the clear plastic in front of the torch. Is the light still bright on the wall?
Now try the baking paper, then the book. Watch the light on the wall each time.
Shine the torch at the mirror and try to make the light bounce onto the wall!

activities.result: Clear plastic lets almost all the light through, baking paper only some, and the book none. The mirror bounces the light to a new place.
activities.why: Transparent lets most light through, translucent lets some, opaque blocks it. Shiny surfaces reflect light.
